extracted.intended_audience: students and readers of natural philosophy / social science (readers of a 19th-century treatise on evolution and social organization)
extracted.subtask_short: chapter on equilibration in organisms and societies
extracted.subtask_description: A textbook-style exposition describing the principle of equilibration (moving equilibrium) as it applies to bodily functions, nervous/mental life, individual adaptation, social/economic organization, and political institutions, with examples and implications for evolution and limits of complexity.

rubrics_metrics.name: Dependent moving equilibrium (organic functions)
rubrics_metrics.description: The organic functions constitute a dependent moving equilibrium — a moving equilibrium, of which the motive power is ever being dissipated ... and is ever being renewed by the taking in of additional motive power.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Functional movements are rhythmical; at each extreme of a rhythm there is progressive equilibration, preservation of a constant mean, and re-establishment of that mean after accidental divergence. Examples: raising an arm (gravity and internal resistance equilibrate motion), heart systole/diastole (momentary equilibrium of muscular strains), circulation (each gush of blood followed by another to maintain momentum). Food is the store of force that replenishes dissipated motive power.

rubrics_metrics.name: Equilibration by antagonistic forces (homeostatic compensation)
rubrics_metrics.description: Any disturbing force that works an excess of change in some direction is gradually diminished and finally neutralized by antagonistic forces which produce a compensating change in the opposite direction, and so, after more or less oscillation, restore the medium condition.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This process explains physiological recovery (vis medicatrix naturae): increased expenditure of motion provokes increased respiration/circulation and increased absorption of food; prolonged draft on reserves produces prolonged rest; even derangements lead to a new mean state if life is not destroyed.

rubrics_metrics.name: Adaptation as equilibration around a new mean
rubrics_metrics.description: When an organ is permanently subject to a new influence, after disturbance there arises a balancing of rhythms around the new average condition produced by this additional influence — this is adaptation.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Increased habitual use raises nutrition and leads to growth until daily waste and repair balance. The cessation of growth marks establishment of balance between daily waste and daily repair. Structural modifications follow functional demands without needing detailed knowledge of re-arrangements.

rubrics_metrics.name: Structural complexity as match to external forces (limit of heterogeneity)
rubrics_metrics.description: The final structural arrangements must be such as will meet all the forces acting on the aggregate, by equivalent antagonist forces; the maintenance of a moving equilibrium requires internal forces corresponding in number, directions, and amounts to the external incident forces.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Functions correlate with organs; amounts of functions with sizes of organs; combinations of functions with organ connections. Thus structural complexity equals having as many specialized parts as are needed to counteract separate and joint external forces. This defines the limit of organic heterogeneity.

rubrics_metrics.name: Equilibration of nervous/mental actions (mental life)
rubrics_metrics.description: Nervous currents are rhythmical; each pulse of nervous force generated moment to moment is met by counteracting forces and is dispersed and equilibrated. Sensations and emotions are expended in bodily changes and stimulation of secreting organs.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Mental processes show rhythms (daily alternation of mental activity and rest), desires reach equilibrium via expenditure in action or imagination, paroxysms of passion return to moderate excitation via counteracting forces. Effort required to call up weakly associated ideas shows resistance; greater energy reduces friction of thought and allows more remote associations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Intellectual equilibration: correspondence of ideas to external relations
rubrics_metrics.description: Each outer connection of phenomena generates, through accumulated experiences, an inner connection of mental states; the result tends to the formation of a mental connection whose relative strength answers to the relative constancy of the physical connection represented.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Over time there is progress towards equilibrium between relations of thought and relations of things: stable external regularities produce strong, indissoluble mental associations; uncertain external relations produce uncertain mental associations. Perfect correspondence would take infinite time and mark the end of further mental evolution.

rubrics_metrics.name: Moral adaptation and habit formation
rubrics_metrics.description: Moral adaptation is a continual approach to equilibrium between emotions and the kinds of conduct necessitated by surrounding conditions; repeated discharge of feeling into action makes that action easier and less repugnant.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Individuals placed permanently in conditions demanding a special kind of action will, via frequent/lengthened performance and reduced resistance, approach a balance between demand and supply of that action. Habits and moral differences of races/nations (across generations) illustrate this progressive adaptation toward equilibrium between constitution and conditions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Social equilibration: population and means of subsistence
rubrics_metrics.description: Each society displays equilibration in adjustment of population to its means of subsistence: species oscillate about an average number the locality can support; abundance increases marriages and numbers, scarcity reduces them, producing rhythmic variations.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Artificial production and improvements change the temporary limit to population, but checking forces operate. Supply and demand are continually adjusted; price represents aggregates of forces. Oscillations in value/rates reflect temporary predominance of forces, settling into a mean unless new influences are added.

rubrics_metrics.name: Industrial/structural equilibration through flows of labour and information
rubrics_metrics.description: Functional equilibrations in society generate structural equilibrations: increased demand for a trade yields higher returns and draws workers until wages fall and resistance across occupations equalizes; diffusion of information and transport improves balance of supply and demand.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Improved roads, printing, railways, telegraphs reduce over- and under-production extremes, produce rapid responses to demand, and narrow oscillations around a uniform mean. Social organization and growth enable closer equilibration of industrial functions; limit tends toward a 'stationary state' when resources and production improvements are exhausted.

rubrics_metrics.name: Political equilibration between individual desires and social institutions
rubrics_metrics.description: Governmental institutions become equilibrated as they harmonize with the desires of the people: antagonistic forces (aggressive, anti-social impulses) and attractive forces (sympathy, union) produce rhythms which settle into a moving equilibrium of comparative regularity.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Small/undeveloped societies show wide oscillations (tribal splits, tyranny followed by license). With development, oscillations moderate (Conservatism vs Reform approximate narrower limits). The ideal limit is a state where individuals have no desires but those satisfiable without exceeding their sphere and society imposes no restraints other than those voluntarily respected — freedom bounded only by the equal freedom of all.

rubrics_metrics.name: Ultimate limit of equilibration (dissipation and death)
rubrics_metrics.description: If equilibration (and with it evolutionary increase of complexity) is incidental to dissipation of force (e.g., solar heat loss), then ultimate equilibration tends to complete rest; the Solar System's dissipating forces suggest a long-term tendency toward omnipresent death.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The text raises the philosophical/scientific question whether continuing dissipation of force (stellar cooling, decrease in geological/biological activity) implies a final universal equilibration (death) even as complexity has been increasing — a problem pointing to limits of evolution and the remote, but inevitable, approach to complete equilibration.
